definition: Flat-panel screen that twists a layer of crystals between two polarizing filters to block or pass light; it cannot make light itself, so it needs a backlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: LCD panel technology whose crystals line up parallel to the glass, giving wide viewing angles and accurate color at a higher cost than older panels.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: Older, low-cost LCD panel technology with fast response times but narrow viewing angles and weaker color, since its crystals twist to let light through.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: LCD panel technology whose crystals stand perpendicular to the glass, giving high contrast and deep blacks but narrower viewing angles than IPS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: Display in which every pixel is a carbon-based compound that glows on its own when current flows, so it needs no backlight and shows true black.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: LCD backlit by thousands of very small LEDs grouped in many local dimming zones, giving higher brightness and contrast than a standard LED-backlit panel.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: Small circuit board in an older laptop screen that converts DC from the motherboard into high-voltage AC for the fluorescent backlight; failure leaves a dark screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: How tightly the dots of a screen are packed, counted per linear inch (PPI); a higher value shows finer detail at the same screen size.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: How many times per second a display redraws its image, measured in hertz; most monitors are 60 Hz, while gaming screens reach 144 or 240 Hz.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: Number of pixels a display shows, written as width by height, for example 1920 x 1080 for Full HD or 3840 x 2160 for 4K.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: The range of colors a display can reproduce; a wider range, as on HDR screens, gives richer and more vivid images.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components

definition: Common Ethernet copper cable of four twisted wire pairs with a plain plastic jacket; cheap but open to EMI, with a 100-meter limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Ethernet copper cable with metal foil or braid around its pairs to resist electromagnetic interference; the shielding must be grounded to work.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Network cable with a fire-resistant, low-smoke jacket, required by fire code in air-handling spaces such as the area above a drop ceiling.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Twisted pair cable with an extra waterproof, protected jacket made to be laid underground outdoors without a separate conduit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Enhanced twisted pair cable rated for 1 Gbps Ethernet up to 100 meters; it replaced the older Cat 5 standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Twisted pair cable rated at 250 MHz that carries 1 Gbps to 100 meters and 10 Gbps over shorter runs of about 55 meters.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: TIA wiring standard for RJ45 ends that starts with white/green on pin 1; one end wired this way and one the other way makes a crossover cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: The most widely used TIA wiring standard for RJ45 ends, starting with white/orange on pin 1; using it on both ends makes a straight-through cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Copper cable with one center conductor, insulation, a braided metal shield, and an outer jacket; RG-6 is used for cable internet and TV.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Optical cable with a very thin core that carries one light path from a laser, used for the longest runs, up to many kilometers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Optical cable with a wider core that carries many light paths, usually from LEDs, used for shorter runs such as server rooms and campus backbones.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Round fiber optic connector with a bayonet mount that is pushed in and twisted to lock in place.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Square fiber optic connector that snaps in and pulls out with a push-pull latch.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Small form factor fiber optic connector, about half the size of SC, with a latch tab; often used in duplex pairs in dense equipment.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals

definition: Eight-pin modular plug (8P8C) that terminates twisted pair Ethernet cable and plugs into network cards, wall jacks, and switches.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Small modular plug with up to six positions, normally using two or four wires, that connects landline phones and DSL modems.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Threaded screw-on connector at the end of RG-6 coaxial cable that attaches to cable modems, TVs, and set-top boxes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Wiring-closet panel where each twisted pair wire is pressed into a metal slot with a special tool instead of using a plug, such as a 66 or 110 block.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals

definition: USB version with a maximum data rate of 480 Mbps, still common for keyboards, mice, and printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: USB version with a maximum data rate of 5 Gbps, often marked by blue ports; later renamed USB 3.2 Gen 1.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Small reversible 24-pin connector that can carry data, video, and high-wattage charging on one cable; now required for new phones in the EU.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Intel interface that combines PCIe and DisplayPort for fast storage and displays; versions 3 and 4 use a USB-C port at 40 Gbps and can daisy-chain devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Cable for the RS-232 standard, usually with a 9-pin DB9 (DE-9) connector, still used to manage network gear and industrial devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Small part that changes one physical connection type to another, for example HDMI to DVI or USB-C to RJ45, without changing the signal format.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Digital audio and video interface for TVs, monitors, and projectors; the standard Type A plug has 19 pins.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Royalty-free digital video and audio interface from VESA with a latching, one-corner-cut plug; a smaller mini version was used on older Macs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors

definition: Video interface with a wide multi-pin connector that carries digital video, plus analog on some versions, but no audio; it is often white.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors

definition: Legacy analog video interface that uses a blue 15-pin DE-15 connector in three rows; it carries no audio.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors

definition: Common internal drive interface with a 7-pin data cable and a 15-pin power connector; revision 3.0 runs at 6 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Shielded external version of the internal drive interface for outside storage enclosures; it carries data only, so the drive needs separate power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

definition: Storage protocol that lets SSDs talk directly over PCIe lanes, usually on an M.2 card, for several times the speed of a SATA SSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

term: Serial Attached Small Computer System Interface
definition: Enterprise drive interface that sends the SCSI command set over serial links; used for server drives, with SAS-4 at 22.5 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Small card-style SSD form factor for older laptops with a single notch on its edge; M.2 has replaced it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Magnetic storage drive with spinning platters and moving read/write heads; 3.5-inch models go in desktops and 2.5-inch models in laptops.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Storage drive with no moving parts that keeps data on non-volatile flash chips, so it is silent, shock-resistant, and much faster than a magnetic disk.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: How fast a magnetic drive's platters turn, in revolutions per minute: 5400 and 7200 RPM are common, and 10,000 or 15,000 RPM suit servers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Small portable NAND storage stick that plugs straight into a USB port, used to move files or boot an installer; eject it before removal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Thin removable flash storage, such as SD or microSD, that slides into a card reader in cameras, phones, and computers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Drive that uses a laser to read and write CDs (about 700 MB), DVDs (4.7 GB per layer), and Blu-ray discs (25 GB per layer).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Disk array that stripes data across two or more drives for speed and full capacity but has no fault tolerance: one failed drive loses everything.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Disk array that mirrors identical copies of data onto two drives, so it survives one drive failure but gives only half the total capacity.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Disk array that stripes data with one set of distributed parity across three or more drives, so it survives the loss of any one drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Disk array that stripes data with two sets of parity across four or more drives, so it survives two drives failing at the same time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Nested disk array of at least four drives that stripes data across mirrored pairs, combining speed with the ability to lose one drive in each pair.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives

definition: Full-size desktop memory stick with separate contacts on each side; DDR4 and DDR5 versions have 288 pins with the notch in different places.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

term: Small outline dual in-line memory module
definition: Shorter memory module used in laptops, mini PCs, and some printers, about half the length of a desktop module.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

definition: Memory technology that moves data on both the rising and falling edges of each clock cycle; its generations (DDR3, DDR4, DDR5) are not interchangeable.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

definition: RAM that stores extra check bits so it can find and fix single-bit errors on the fly; used in servers and needs board support.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

definition: Memory setup that uses two 64-bit paths at once for a 128-bit bus; matched modules go in the same-colored slots.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

definition: Memory setup that needs four identical modules, one in each bank, so four 64-bit paths work together; with fewer modules it falls back.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM

definition: The standard full-size motherboard form factor, 12 x 9.6 inches, with RAM slots at right angles to the expansion slots and a 24-pin power connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Smaller square motherboard form factor, up to 9.6 x 9.6 inches, that fits in larger cases but has fewer expansion and RAM slots.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Family of small, low-power motherboard form factors created by VIA, including Mini, Nano, Pico, and Mobile sizes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Older 32-bit parallel expansion bus with a shared bandwidth of about 266 MB/s, now mostly replaced by its serial successor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Serial point-to-point expansion bus that sends data over lanes; slots come in x1, x4, x8, and x16 sizes, and x16 is used for video cards.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Group of small pins at the edge of a motherboard that the case's power button, reset button, and LED wires plug into.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: CPU socket with spring pins in the socket that touch flat contacts on the processor; used by Intel and AMD's AM5.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: CPU socket with holes that accept pins on the underside of the processor, locked by a lever; used by older AMD sockets such as AM4.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Board with two or more processor sockets so several CPUs work together, common in servers and high-end workstations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Expansion card that turns digital data into audio, with color-coded 3.5 mm jacks: lime green for speakers, pink for a microphone, light blue for line in.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Expansion card with its own GPU and memory that drives monitors; usually goes in a PCIe x16 slot and may need 6- or 8-pin power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Expansion card that records video or audio from an outside source, such as a camera or game console, for editing or streaming.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Expansion card that connects a computer to external storage such as a storage area network, often over Fibre Channel with LC connectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Legacy motherboard firmware with a keyboard-driven text setup program that tests hardware and starts the operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Modern motherboard firmware that replaced the legacy type; it has a mouse-driven setup, faster startup, GPT drive support, and Secure Boot.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware setting that lists the order of devices to start from, such as SSD, USB, optical, or network; put the system drive first after installing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware feature that reads sensors on the CPU, GPU, and chipset and can raise fan speed, warn, or shut down at a set limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware setting that sets how fast fans on the motherboard headers spin, by RPM or by profiles such as silent, optimal, or full.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: UEFI feature that loads only boot loaders with a trusted digital signature, which blocks rootkits and tampered operating system loaders.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware password that a person must enter before the computer will load the operating system.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware administrator password that protects the setup utility, so only authorized people can change the firmware settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Firmware setting that can turn off USB ports or stop booting from USB drives, which helps block attacks with infected drives left in public.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Chip on the motherboard that creates and stores encryption keys for full-drive encryption such as BitLocker; Windows 11 needs version 2.0.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards

definition: Separate device, such as a USB key, adapter card, or network appliance, with a cryptoprocessor that creates, stores, and manages digital keys.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory

definition: Low-power processor architecture with a small, simple instruction set, used in smartphones, tablets, and some laptops because it runs cool and efficiently.
acceptedAnswers: Advanced Reduced Instruction Set Computer Machine
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: CPU package that holds two or more physical processing units that work at the same time, giving more work done with less heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Technology that lets one core run two instruction streams at once, so the operating system sees two logical processors for each physical core.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Finned block of aluminum or copper that sits on a CPU or chip and draws heat away by conduction; an active one has a fan on it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Compound spread thinly between a CPU and its cooler to fill tiny gaps in the metal; clean off and reapply it each time the cooler is removed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Soft, pre-formed sheet of heat-conducting material, often factory-applied to a cooler or used on memory chips and M.2 drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Fan mounted in the computer chassis that moves air through it; front fans pull cool air in, while rear and top fans push hot air out.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Cooling system that pumps coolant through a block on the CPU or GPU to a radiator with fans; the most effective method, but it can leak.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs

definition: Setup of two or more power units in one system, each with its own cord, so if one fails the other carries the load with no downtime.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

definition: Power supply whose cables plug into ports on the unit, so only the cables a build needs are attached, for neater cable management.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

definition: The maximum power a power supply can deliver; it should be higher than the total draw of all components, or the system may reboot or fail to start.

definition: Energy efficiency rating that a power supply converts at least 80 percent of AC input to DC, with Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Titanium levels.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

definition: Switch on the back of older power supplies to set the input to 115 VAC (110–120 V, as in the US) or 230 VAC (220–240 V, as in Europe).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

definition: Main power plug from the supply to an ATX motherboard, built as 20+4 so the extra four pins can detach for older 20-pin boards.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

definition: Older four-pin power plug with two beveled corners that supplies 5 V and 12 V to legacy PATA drives, optical drives, and fans.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

definition: Thin 15-pin L-shaped power plug that supplies 3.3 V, 5 V, and 12 V to internal storage drives.

source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

definition: Power supply output that carries the most load, feeding the CPU, video card, fans, and drive motors.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

definition: Power supply output that feeds drive logic boards and USB ports; a standby version stays on whenever the PC is plugged in.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

definition: Lowest power supply output, used by RAM, the chipset, and some expansion cards and drives, and present on the SATA power plug.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies

definition: HP page description language used by the most common printer drivers, fast and suited to everyday office documents and spreadsheets.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Adobe page description language that describes a page independently of the device, preferred for professional graphics, desktop publishing, and presentations.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Embedded software that controls a printer's hardware; update it from the maker's site or the embedded web page to fix bugs and security flaws.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Windows feature that makes a printer attached to one PC available to others on the network; that host computer must stay on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Print setting that puts output on both sides of each sheet, either automatically with a special assembly or manually by refeeding paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Print setting that chooses portrait (tall) or landscape (wide) layout for the page.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Printer configuration that tells the device which paper size and type, such as letter, legal, or envelopes, is loaded in each paper source.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Printer setting for output resolution in dots per inch, offered as draft, normal, or best; 600 DPI or higher is letter quality.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Single office machine that can print, scan, copy, and often fax, usually connected to the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Scanner part that pulls a stack of loose pages through one at a time for copying or scanning, without placing each on the glass.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Scanner with a glass surface under a lid where one page, photo, or open book is laid face down to be scanned.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Network scan service that sends the scanned file, usually a PDF, to a recipient as an attachment through a mail server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

definition: Network scan service that saves the scanned file into a shared folder on a server over SMB, useful when the file is too large to email.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

definition: Network scan service that uploads the scanned file straight to an online storage service, such as OneDrive or Google Drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Printer security that makes a person log in at the device with credentials or a PIN before printing, copying, or scanning.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

definition: Printer security in which users identify themselves by tapping or swiping an ID card on a reader attached to the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

definition: Record a printer or print server keeps of who printed what, when, and on which device; it usually must be enabled first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers

definition: Print option that holds a job at the device until the user arrives and enters a passcode, so sensitive pages are not left in the tray.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices

definition: Page printer that uses a laser to draw the image on a charged drum, then fuses powdered toner onto paper with heat; common in offices.

definition: Printer that sprays tiny drops of liquid ink through nozzles in a moving head onto paper, common in homes for color photos.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Printer that makes images by heating specially coated paper with a heating element, used for receipts at point-of-sale systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Printer that strikes an inked ribbon against the paper with pins or formed characters, the only kind that can print multipart forms.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Laser printer consumable that holds the powdered pigment and plastic, often with the drum built in; remove the sealing tape before installing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Set of replacement laser printer parts, such as a fuser and rollers, applied at a set page count; reset the counter afterward.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Light-sensitive cylinder in a laser printer that is charged, written on by the laser, and coated with toner before the image moves to paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Laser printer part with heated, pressurized rollers, around 200 °C, that melt toner onto the paper; if it fails, prints smear when rubbed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Printer routine that aligns the printing mechanism with the paper and adjusts color and margins, run after replacing cartridges or a maintenance kit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Replaceable reservoir of liquid ink in an inkjet printer, one for black and one or more for colors; some printers stop when one runs dry.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Part that moves across the page and puts the image on paper: nozzles in an inkjet, or a row of pins in an impact printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Rubber cylinder that grabs paper from the tray and moves it through the printer; clean or replace it when pages misfeed or jam.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Specially coated paper that darkens where heat touches it; store it away from sunlight and heat, which turn it dark.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Part of a thermal printer that heats spots on the coated paper to form text; clean it during maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Thermal printer mechanism, including the rubber platen roller, that pulls the paper roll between itself and the heated print head.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Inked fabric strip in an impact printer that the pins strike to transfer ink onto the paper; replace it when print gets faint.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance

definition: Stacked forms with carbon or carbonless layers, so one strike prints an original and copies; only impact printers can use it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance
